title: NEET UG 2026 - Set 4: Dark Horse Topics (Surprise Questions)
description: 180 MCQs from lesser-tested topics that are statistically due for appearance in 2026. Includes chapters skipped in 2023-2024, new NEP-pattern questions, and topics with irregular appearance cycles.

deep_analysis.methodology: Topics that appeared in 2020-2021 but were absent in 2023-2024, chapters with low recent frequency but high NCERT weightage, and new pattern questions expected under NEP
dark_horse_physics: Communication Systems (often skipped but in syllabus)
Motion in a Plane: Relative motion in rain/river
dark_horse_chemistry: Redox Reactions: Balancing by ion-electron method
dark_horse_biology: Microbes in Human Welfare: detailed applications

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a prism of angle A = 60° and minimum deviation δm = 30°, the refractive index of the prism material is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Dispersion without deviation can be achieved by combining two prisms such that:
options: Net deviation is zero but angular dispersion exists
Both deviation and dispersion are zero
questions.explanation: A combination of crown and flint glass prisms can produce dispersion without deviation (achromatic combination in reverse).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In amplitude modulation, the bandwidth of the modulated signal is:
questions.explanation: AM bandwidth = (fc + fm) - (fc - fm) = 2fm. The modulated signal occupies 2fm bandwidth around carrier.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The maximum range of a TV transmission tower of height h is: (R = radius of Earth)
questions.explanation: Line-of-sight distance: d = √(2Rh). This is the maximum distance up to which the signal can reach along the curved Earth surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Wien's displacement law, the wavelength of maximum emission from a black body at temperature T is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation: Wien's law: λmax × T = b (constant = 2.898×10⁻³ m·K). λmax ∝ 1/T.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A black body at temperature T₁ radiates energy E. If temperature is increased to 2T₁, the energy radiated becomes:
questions.explanation: Stefan's law: E ∝ T⁴. E₂/E₁ = (2T₁)⁴/T₁⁴ = 16. E₂ = 16E

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio of longitudinal strain to lateral strain is called:
questions.explanation: Poisson's ratio (σ) = lateral strain/longitudinal strain (note: the question asks what the ratio of long/lat is called - it's actually the inverse; Poisson's ratio = lat/long). Actually Poisson's ratio = lateral strain/longitudinal strain. The correct answer is Poisson's ratio as it defines this relationship.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wire of length 2m and cross-sectional area 10⁻⁶ m² is stretched by 0.1 mm under a load. If Young's modulus is 2×10¹¹ N/m², the load applied is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The power factor of a series LCR circuit at resonance is:
questions.explanation: At resonance: XL = XC, impedance Z = R (minimum). Power factor cos φ = R/Z = R/R = 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A transformer has 500 turns in primary and 5000 turns in secondary. If the primary voltage is 20V, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Vs = Vp × Ns/Np = 20 × 5000/500 = 200V (step-up transformer).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Rain is falling vertically with velocity 10 m/s. A man walks with 10 m/s. He should hold his umbrella at angle with vertical equal to:
questions.explanation: tan θ = v_man/v_rain = 10/10 = 1. θ = 45° with the vertical (tilted in direction of motion).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A boat can travel at 5 km/h in still water. A river flows at 3 km/h. The time taken to cross a 4 km wide river by shortest path is:
questions.explanation: For shortest path: boat must travel at angle. Component across river = √(5²-3²) = 4 km/h. Time = 4/4 = 1 hour.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A bimetallic strip made of brass and iron is heated. The strip will bend with:
questions.explanation: Brass has higher coefficient of expansion than iron. On heating, brass expands more → brass goes to the outer (convex) side.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: 10 g of ice at 0°C is mixed with 10 g of water at 100°C. The final temperature of the mixture is: (L_ice = 80 cal/g, specific heat of water = 1 cal/g/°C)
questions.explanation: Heat needed to melt ice = 10×80 = 800 cal. Heat available from water = 10×1×100 = 1000 cal. After melting: 1000-800 = 200 cal heats 20g water. ΔT = 200/(20×1) = 10°C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A source of sound of frequency 500 Hz moves towards a stationary observer with velocity 30 m/s. The apparent frequency heard by observer is: (Speed of sound = 330 m/s)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of the third overtone is how many times the fundamental?
questions.explanation: Closed pipe: only odd harmonics. Fundamental = f. First overtone = 3f, second = 5f, third overtone = 7f. Answer = 7 times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A thin film of oil (μ=1.4) on water appears coloured in white light. This is due to:
questions.explanation: Thin film interference: light reflected from top and bottom surfaces of oil film interfere. Different wavelengths show constructive interference at different thicknesses → colours.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Brewster's angle for a glass surface of refractive index √3 is:
questions.explanation: tan(iB) = μ = √3. iB = 60°. At Brewster's angle, reflected light is completely polarised.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The terminal velocity of a sphere falling through a viscous liquid is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity vt = 2r²(ρ-σ)g/9η. vt ∝ r² (Stokes' law).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The radius of gyration of a uniform rod of length L about an axis through its center perpendicular to its length is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric field on the axial line of a dipole at large distance r varies as:
questions.explanation: For a dipole, E_axial = 2kp/r³ (at large r >> l). Electric field varies as 1/r³ for dipole (unlike 1/r² for point charge).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The graph of maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons vs frequency of incident radiation is a straight line with slope equal to:
questions.explanation: KE_max = hν - φ. This is y = mx + c form. Slope = h (Planck's constant). Y-intercept = -φ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The magnetic field at the center of a circular coil of N turns, radius R, carrying current I is:
questions.explanation: B at center of N-turn circular coil = Nμ₀I/2R (superposition of N single-turn coils).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a nuclear fusion reaction: ²₁H + ²₁H → ³₂He + ¹₀n, if the mass defect is 0.0024 amu, the energy released per fusion is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The Boolean expression for a NAND gate is:
questions.explanation: NAND = NOT + AND. Output Y = (A·B)' = A̅+B̅ (De Morgan's). NAND is universal gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius R with constant speed v. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration = v²/R, always directed towards the centre of the circular path (perpendicular to velocity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A capacitor of 10μF charged to 500V is connected to another uncharged capacitor of 10μF. The energy lost during charge sharing is:
questions.explanation: Initial energy = ½×10⁻⁵×500² = 1.25J. Final: V = 250V, E = ½×2×10⁻⁵×250² = 0.625J. Loss = 0.625J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: By the parallel axis theorem, if moment of inertia about center of mass is I_cm, then about a parallel axis at distance d is:
questions.explanation: Parallel axis theorem: I = I_cm + Md² where M is total mass and d is distance between the two parallel axes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The angle of dip at the magnetic equator is:
questions.explanation: At magnetic equator, the Earth's magnetic field is horizontal (no vertical component). Angle of dip = 0°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The phenomenon of self-induction is the basis of:
questions.explanation: Self-induction: changing current induces EMF in the same coil opposing the change. Inductor/choke coil is based on this principle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Photons of wavelength λ and energy E. If wavelength is halved, the momentum of each photon becomes:
questions.explanation: p = h/λ. If λ → λ/2, then p → h/(λ/2) = 2h/λ = 2p. Momentum doubles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between 600K and 300K is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a reflecting telescope, the objective is a:
questions.explanation: Reflecting (Cassegrain) telescope uses a concave mirror as objective. Advantages: no chromatic aberration, can be made large, lighter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric potential at a point on the equatorial line of a dipole is:
questions.explanation: On equatorial line, the potentials due to +q and -q cancel (equal magnitude, opposite sign). V_equatorial = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an NPN transistor in active mode, the collector current is related to emitter current as:
options: IC ≈ IE (IC is slightly less than IE)
questions.explanation: In active mode: IE = IC + IB. Since IB is very small (~1-2% of IE), IC ≈ IE (about 98% of IE). α = IC/IE ≈ 0.98.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a string fixed at both ends is 200 Hz. If the tension is increased to 4 times, the new fundamental frequency is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The dimension of angular momentum is same as:
questions.explanation: Angular momentum = [ML²T⁻¹]. Planck's constant h = E/ν = [ML²T⁻¹]. Same dimensions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The colour code of a resistor shows: Brown, Black, Orange. The resistance value is:
questions.explanation: Brown=1, Black=0, Orange=10³. Resistance = 10 × 10³ = 10,000 Ω = 10 kΩ

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two thin lenses of focal lengths f₁ and f₂ separated by distance d have equivalent focal length given by:
questions.explanation: For two lenses separated by d: 1/f = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ - d/(f₁f₂). When d=0, reduces to simple combination formula.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The time period of a satellite in a circular orbit depends on:
questions.explanation: Kepler's 3rd law: T² ∝ r³. T = 2π√(r³/GM). Time period depends on orbital radius and mass of central body, NOT on satellite's mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The angle of contact for mercury-glass interface is:
questions.explanation: Mercury doesn't wet glass → meniscus is convex → angle of contact is obtuse (~140°). For water-glass it's acute (~0°).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The mean free path of gas molecules depends on:
questions.explanation: Mean free path λ = 1/(√2 πnd²) where n = number density, d = molecular diameter. Inversely proportional to both.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The phenomenon of echo requires a minimum distance of the reflecting surface from the source to be: (speed of sound = 340 m/s)
questions.explanation: Echo persistence time = 0.1s. Total distance = v×t = 340×0.1 = 34m. One-way distance = 34/2 = 17m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A hollow metallic sphere of radius R is charged with charge Q. The electric field inside the sphere is:
questions.explanation: Inside a charged conducting sphere, electric field is zero (charges reside on outer surface; by Gauss's law, enclosed charge = 0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Wattless current flows in a circuit containing only:
questions.explanation: Wattless current: when phase difference = 90° (power = 0). This occurs in pure L or pure C circuits. P = VI cos90° = 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is classified as:
questions.explanation: Aspirin is an analgesic (pain reliever) and antipyretic (reduces fever). It inhibits prostaglandin synthesis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cimetidine is an example of:
questions.explanation: Cimetidine is an H₂ receptor blocker/antacid. It inhibits histamine-stimulated gastric acid secretion (used for peptic ulcers).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Soap is sodium/potassium salt of:
questions.explanation: Soap = sodium/potassium salt of long chain fatty acid (C₁₂-C₁₈). e.g., Sodium stearate (C₁₇H₃₅COONa).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Lanthanoid contraction is caused by:
questions.explanation: Lanthanoid contraction: 4f electrons have poor shielding → effective nuclear charge increases → size decreases across the series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The most common oxidation state of lanthanoids is:
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids most commonly show +3 oxidation state. Some show +2 (Eu²⁺) or +4 (Ce⁴⁺) for extra stability of empty/half-filled/full 4f orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives:
questions.explanation: Sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) on hydrolysis: Sucrose → Glucose + Fructose. The mixture is called invert sugar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cellulose is a polymer of:
questions.explanation: Cellulose: linear polymer of β-D-glucose units linked by β(1→4) glycosidic bonds. Starch has α-D-glucose with α(1→4) bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen peroxide acts as both oxidizing and reducing agent because:
options: Oxygen in H₂O₂ is in -1 oxidation state (intermediate)
questions.explanation: In H₂O₂, O is in -1 state. It can be reduced to -2 (oxidizing agent) or oxidized to 0 (reducing agent). Intermediate oxidation state allows both.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Permanent hardness of water is due to presence of:
options: Chlorides and sulphates of Ca and Mg
questions.explanation: Permanent hardness: CaCl₂, MgCl₂, CaSO₄, MgSO₄ (not removed by boiling). Temporary = bicarbonates (removed by boiling).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a disproportionation reaction, the same element is:
questions.explanation: Disproportionation: same element in one oxidation state → two different states (one higher, one lower). e.g., 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An emulsion of oil in water is stabilized by:
questions.explanation: Oil in water (O/W) emulsion stabilized by hydrophilic (water-loving) emulsifiers like soap, proteins. They reduce surface tension.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Gold sol prepared by Bredig's arc method is:
questions.explanation: Metal sols (gold, silver) are lyophobic colloids (solvent-hating). They need stabilizers, are irreversible, and easily coagulated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Lassaigne's test is used to detect:
options: N, S, and halogens in organic compounds
questions.explanation: Lassaigne's test: organic compound + Na → NaCN (if N present), Na₂S (if S), NaX (if halogen). Detects N, S, X in organic compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Standard enthalpy of combustion is always:
questions.explanation: Combustion is always exothermic (releases heat). Therefore, ΔH°combustion is always negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The EAN (Effective Atomic Number) rule was given by:
questions.explanation: Sidgwick's EAN rule: metal in complex tends to acquire electrons until its total electron count equals the nearest noble gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Saytzeff's rule predicts the major product of E1 elimination to be:
questions.explanation: Saytzeff (Zaitsev) rule: β-elimination preferentially gives the more substituted (more stable) alkene as major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A catalyst works by:
options: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
questions.explanation: Catalyst lowers Ea (activation energy) by providing alternative mechanism. It doesn't change ΔG, ΔH, or equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Le Chatelier's principle states that when a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to:
options: Counteract the change and restore equilibrium
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier: if equilibrium is disturbed (concentration, pressure, temperature), system shifts to oppose the change and establish new equilibrium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Henry's law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is:
options: Directly proportional to its partial pressure
questions.explanation: Henry's law: p = KH × x (partial pressure ∝ mole fraction in solution). Higher pressure → more gas dissolves.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The element with the highest electron affinity is:
questions.explanation: Chlorine has highest electron affinity (-349 kJ/mol), not fluorine (-328 kJ/mol). F is small → electron-electron repulsion in 2p reduces its EA.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Fries rearrangement converts phenyl ester to:
questions.explanation: Fries rearrangement: phenyl ester + AlCl₃ → o-hydroxyacetophenone + p-hydroxyacetophenone (acyl group migrates to ring).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Perkin's reaction is used to synthesize:
questions.explanation: Perkin's reaction: ArCHO + (CH₃CO)₂O + CH₃COONa → ArCH=CHCOOH (cinnamic acid from benzaldehyde).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The purple colour of KMnO₄ is due to:
questions.explanation: KMnO₄: Mn in +7 (d⁰) has no d electrons for d-d transition. The colour is due to charge transfer (ligand to metal).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Tollen's reagent is:
questions.explanation: Tollen's reagent = [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ (ammoniacal AgNO₃). Gives silver mirror with aldehydes (not ketones).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: PTFE (Teflon) is a polymer of:
questions.explanation: PTFE (Teflon) = poly(tetrafluoroethylene). Monomer: CF₂=CF₂. Non-stick, chemically inert, high thermal stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reagent used in Swern oxidation of alcohols is:
questions.explanation: Swern oxidation: DMSO + (COCl)₂ + Et₃N converts 1° alcohol → aldehyde, 2° alcohol → ketone (mild, no over-oxidation).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Frenkel defect is most common in compounds with:
questions.explanation: Frenkel defect: smaller ion (usually cation) moves to interstitial site. Common when cation-anion size difference is large (e.g., AgBr, ZnS).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a lead storage battery, during discharge at cathode:
questions.explanation: Cathode (reduction) during discharge: PbO₂ + 4H⁺ + SO₄²⁻ + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. PbO₂ reduced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The type of bond present in CsCl crystal is:
questions.explanation: CsCl is an ionic compound (Cs⁺ and Cl⁻ held by electrostatic attraction). It has BCC-type structure (not actually BCC of identical atoms).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because:
options: Phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance
questions.explanation: Phenoxide (C₆H₅O⁻) is resonance-stabilized (negative charge delocalized over benzene ring). Ethoxide has no such stabilization → phenol is more acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The allotrope of carbon that is the hardest known natural substance is:
questions.explanation: Diamond: each carbon sp³ hybridized, bonded to 4 others in tetrahedral arrangement → 3D network → hardest natural substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In electrophilic aromatic substitution, -OH group is:
questions.explanation: -OH is ortho/para director and ring activator (due to +M effect > -I effect). Electron donation to ring increases reactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hess's law is a consequence of:
questions.explanation: Hess's law: total enthalpy change is independent of path (only depends on initial and final states). This is because H is a state function.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Kolbe's reaction is the carboxylation of:
options: Sodium phenoxide with CO₂ to give salicylic acid
questions.explanation: Kolbe's reaction: C₆H₅ONa + CO₂ (125°C, 4-7 atm) → sodium salicylate → H⁺ → salicylic acid (o-hydroxybenzoic acid).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Rosenmund reduction converts:
questions.explanation: Rosenmund reduction: RCOCl + H₂/Pd-BaSO₄ → RCHO. Pd poisoned with BaSO₄ prevents over-reduction to alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Back bonding in BF₃ involves overlap of:
options: Filled p-orbital of F with empty p-orbital of B
questions.explanation: In BF₃: F has lone pair in 2p orbital that overlaps with empty 2p orbital of B (pπ-pπ back bonding). This makes B-F bond shorter.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Benedict's solution is used to test for:
questions.explanation: Benedict's solution (Cu²⁺ citrate complex) → reduced by reducing sugars (glucose, fructose) → red Cu₂O precipitate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The common ion effect is an application of:
questions.explanation: Common ion effect: adding a common ion shifts equilibrium (Le Chatelier's principle) to reduce its concentration → decreases dissociation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An azeotropic mixture boils at a constant temperature because:
options: Liquid and vapour phases have same composition
questions.explanation: Azeotrope: composition of liquid = composition of vapour. Cannot be separated by simple distillation. Boils at constant T like a pure substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Reimer-Tiemann reaction on phenol gives:
questions.explanation: Reimer-Tiemann: Phenol + CHCl₃ + NaOH → Salicylaldehyde (ortho product). Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) is the electrophile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The oxidation number of Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Fittig reaction involves coupling of:
questions.explanation: Fittig: 2ArX + 2Na → Ar-Ar + 2NaX. Coupling of two aryl halides. Wurtz-Fittig = ArX + RX + 2Na → Ar-R.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Interstitial compounds of transition metals are characteristically:
options: Very hard, high melting point, chemically inert
questions.explanation: Interstitial compounds: small atoms (H, C, N, B) occupy voids in metal lattice. Properties: extremely hard, very high MP, chemically inert, metallic conductors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hoffman elimination of quaternary ammonium hydroxide gives the:
questions.explanation: Hofmann elimination: quaternary ammonium → less substituted alkene (anti-Zaitsev). Due to bulky leaving group, E2 occurs at less hindered β-H.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of phenol with bromine water gives:
questions.explanation: Phenol + Br₂(aq) → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white ppt) + 3HBr. The -OH group activates the ring so strongly that all three positions are brominated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: MOET (Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer) is a programme for:
options: Increasing herd size of superior cattle
questions.explanation: MOET: cow given FSH for superovulation → mated → 8-32 embryos recovered → transferred to surrogate mothers. Rapid herd improvement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yielding exotic breed of cow?
questions.explanation: Jersey is a high-yielding exotic (foreign) breed. Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, and Gir are Indian (indigenous) breeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The microorganism used in the production of citric acid commercially is:
questions.explanation: Aspergillus niger (a fungus) is used for commercial production of citric acid by fermentation of molasses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Biogas is produced by:
questions.explanation: Methanogens (Methanobacterium, Methanococcus) produce methane (biogas) by anaerobic digestion of organic waste in biogas plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressant produced by:
questions.explanation: Cyclosporin A from Trichoderma polysporum (fungus) is used as immunosuppressant in organ transplant patients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Green revolution in India is associated with:
options: Development of high-yielding wheat and rice varieties
questions.explanation: Green Revolution (1960s-70s): high-yielding varieties of wheat (by Norman Borlaug) and rice introduced in India → dramatic increase in food production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mineral element required for nitrogen fixation by Rhizobium is:
questions.explanation: Molybdenum (Mo) is a component of nitrogenase enzyme (Mo-Fe protein) essential for biological nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chlorosis (yellowing of leaves) is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Chlorosis: deficiency of N, Mg, Fe, Mn, Zn, S (all needed for chlorophyll synthesis or function). Most common: N and Fe deficiency.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lymph differs from blood in that it:
questions.explanation: Lymph: colorless, lacks RBCs, has fewer proteins than blood, but has lymphocytes (WBCs). Formed from tissue fluid entering lymph capillaries.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Rh factor is named after:
questions.explanation: Rh factor discovered by Landsteiner and Wiener (1940) in Rhesus monkey blood. About 80% humans are Rh positive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Uricotelic organisms excrete nitrogenous waste as:
questions.explanation: Uricotelic: excrete uric acid (insoluble, non-toxic, least water needed). Birds, reptiles, land insects. Adaptation to conserve water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Osteoporosis is caused by:
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis: decreased bone mass/density (especially in post-menopausal women due to decreased estrogen). Bones become brittle and fracture-prone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Rigor mortis is due to:
options: Formation of permanent cross-bridges (no ATP for detachment)
questions.explanation: After death, ATP depletes → actin-myosin cross-bridges cannot detach → muscles become rigid (rigor mortis). Resolves when proteins degrade.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ethylene is the plant hormone that:
questions.explanation: Ethylene (C₂H₄): gaseous hormone, promotes fruit ripening, leaf abscission, senescence, breaking seed dormancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The respiratory quotient (RQ) for carbohydrates is:
questions.explanation: RQ = CO₂ released/O₂ consumed. For carbohydrates: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O. RQ = 6/6 = 1.0. For fats RQ < 1 (~0.7).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transduction in bacteria is gene transfer mediated by:
questions.explanation: Transduction: transfer of genetic material from one bacterium to another through bacteriophage (virus as vector). Discovered by Zinder & Lederberg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sacred groves are examples of:
questions.explanation: Sacred groves: forest patches protected by tribal communities due to religious beliefs. In-situ conservation (in natural habitat). Found across India.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Red Data Book is maintained by:
questions.explanation: IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) maintains the Red Data Book/Red List documenting endangered, vulnerable, and extinct species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hormone that stimulates milk ejection (let-down reflex) is:
questions.explanation: Oxytocin (from posterior pituitary) causes milk ejection by contracting myoepithelial cells of mammary glands. Prolactin stimulates milk production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Diabetes insipidus is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Diabetes insipidus: lack of ADH → kidneys cannot reabsorb water → excessive dilute urine (polyuria) and excessive thirst. Not related to blood sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Griffith's transformation experiment (1928) showed that:
options: There exists a 'transforming principle' that can change bacterial phenotype
questions.explanation: Griffith showed S-strain (virulent, killed) could transform R-strain (non-virulent) to S-strain → a 'transforming principle' exists. Avery later identified it as DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Apomixis is seed formation:
questions.explanation: Apomixis: seed formation without fertilization. Embryo develops from diploid egg or nucellar cells. Genetically identical to parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oogamy is the type of sexual reproduction found in:
options: Volvox, Fucus, and all higher plants
questions.explanation: Oogamy: fusion of large non-motile egg with small motile sperm. Found in Volvox, Fucus, all bryophytes, pteridophytes, and seed plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bioluminescence is well known in:
questions.explanation: Ctenophora (comb jellies/sea walnuts) are well known for bioluminescence. They have comb-like ciliated plates for locomotion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nitrogen fixation is the conversion of:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen fixation: N₂ + 8H⁺ + 8e⁻ + 16ATP → 2NH₃ + H₂ + 16ADP. Catalyzed by nitrogenase in Rhizobium, Azotobacter, cyanobacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term 'biological clock' or circadian rhythm is controlled by:
options: Suprachiasmatic nucleus of hypothalamus (with pineal gland)
questions.explanation: Circadian rhythm (24-hr biological clock) is controlled by suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) in hypothalamus. Pineal gland secretes melatonin for sleep-wake cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plasmodesmata are:
options: Cytoplasmic connections between adjacent plant cells
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata: cytoplasmic strands passing through cell walls connecting adjacent plant cells. Allow cell-to-cell communication (symplastic pathway).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Biomagnification refers to:
options: Increase in concentration of non-degradable pollutants at successive trophic levels
questions.explanation: Biomagnification: non-biodegradable substances (DDT, mercury) accumulate increasingly at higher trophic levels (e.g., DDT in fish-eating birds).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Penicillin was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming (1928) discovered penicillin from Penicillium notatum (fungus). First antibiotic used clinically (1940s by Florey & Chain).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP) is used in:
questions.explanation: RFLP: differences in DNA fragment lengths after restriction enzyme digestion. Used for DNA fingerprinting, genetic mapping, and forensics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nematocysts (cnidoblasts) are characteristic of phylum:
questions.explanation: Nematocysts (stinging cells/cnidocytes) are unique to Cnidaria (Hydra, jellyfish, corals). Used for defense and prey capture.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Adaptive radiation is best exemplified by:
questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation: single ancestor → diversification into multiple species filling different niches. Best example: Darwin's finches (different beak shapes for different food).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Metastasis in cancer refers to:
options: Spread of cancer cells to distant sites via blood/lymph
questions.explanation: Metastasis: malignant cells break away from primary tumor, travel through blood/lymph, and establish secondary tumors at distant sites.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gibberellins were first discovered from:
questions.explanation: Gibberellins first extracted from fungus Gibberella fujikuroi (causes 'bakane'/foolish seedling disease in rice). Promote stem elongation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Microsporogenesis results in formation of:
questions.explanation: Microsporogenesis: microspore mother cell (2n) → meiosis → 4 haploid microspores (tetrad). Each microspore develops into a pollen grain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Semi-autonomous organelles that contain their own DNA are:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own circular DNA, ribosomes (70S), and can self-replicate. Called semi-autonomous (still depend on nuclear genes).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Rods and cones in the retina contain:
questions.explanation: Rods: rhodopsin (scotopsin + retinal) for dim light vision. Cones: iodopsin (photopsin + retinal) for color vision and bright light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The region of the Earth where life exists is called:
questions.explanation: Biosphere: the sum total of all ecosystems; the zone of life on Earth (includes parts of lithosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The minimum distance between two genes on the same chromosome is expressed in:
questions.explanation: Genetic distance measured in centiMorgans (cM) or map units. 1 cM = 1% recombination frequency between two genes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Metameric segmentation is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Metameric segmentation: body divided into segments (metameres), each with repetition of organs. Found in Annelida (earthworm: ~100-120 segments).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phyllotaxy refers to:
options: Arrangement of leaves on the stem
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy: pattern of leaf arrangement on stem. Types: alternate (1 leaf/node), opposite (2 leaves/node), whorled (3+ leaves/node).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Acetylcholine is a neurotransmitter released at:
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine (ACh): released at neuromuscular junctions (motor end plate), parasympathetic endings, and some CNS synapses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Interkinesis is the stage between:
questions.explanation: Interkinesis: short resting phase between meiosis I and II. No DNA replication occurs during this period. Cells remain haploid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Biopiracy refers to:
options: Unauthorized exploitation of biological resources and traditional knowledge
questions.explanation: Biopiracy: exploitation of biological resources and indigenous knowledge without proper authorization or benefit sharing (e.g., patenting neem, turmeric, basmati).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Philadelphia chromosome is associated with:
questions.explanation: Philadelphia chromosome: reciprocal translocation t(9;22). BCR-ABL fusion gene produces constitutively active tyrosine kinase → CML.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) plants fix CO₂ during:
questions.explanation: CAM plants (succulents): stomata open at night → fix CO₂ into malate (OAA→malate). Day: stomata closed, malate → CO₂ → Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Universal donor blood group is:
questions.explanation: O negative: no A, B antigens (no agglutination) and no Rh antigen. Can donate to all blood groups → universal donor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is related to:
questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol: international treaty to phase out production of ozone-depleting substances (CFCs, halons, carbon tetrachloride).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: BOD (Biological Oxygen Demand) is a measure of:
questions.explanation: BOD: amount of dissolved oxygen needed by microorganisms to decompose organic matter in water. High BOD = more pollution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman with blood group A (genotype I^A i) marries a man with blood group B (genotype I^B i). The possible blood groups of their children are:
options: A, B, AB, O (all four possible)
questions.explanation: I^A i × I^B i → I^A I^B (AB), I^A i (A), I^B i (B), ii (O). All four blood groups possible in offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Signal recognition particle (SRP) is involved in:
questions.explanation: SRP recognizes signal peptide on nascent polypeptide → halts translation → directs ribosome to ER membrane → protein enters ER lumen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Elephantiasis (filariasis) is caused by:
questions.explanation: Elephantiasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti/W. malayi (nematode). Transmitted by Culex mosquito. Blocks lymph vessels → limb swelling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cleistogamous flowers ensure:
questions.explanation: Cleistogamous flowers: remain closed, never open → guaranteed self-pollination. Found in Oxalis, Commelina, Viola.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bulliform cells (motor cells) are found in:
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells: large, bubble-shaped cells in upper epidermis of monocot (grass) leaves. They lose water → leaf rolls to reduce transpiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Meselson and Stahl experiment proved:
questions.explanation: Meselson-Stahl (1958) used ¹⁵N/¹⁴N labeled E. coli DNA and density gradient centrifugation to prove semiconservative DNA replication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The net gain of ATP from one molecule of glucose in aerobic respiration (considering theoretical maximum) is:
questions.explanation: Glycolysis: 2 ATP + 2 NADH. Pyruvate decarboxylation: 2 NADH. Krebs: 2 ATP + 6 NADH + 2 FADH₂. ETC: NADH=2.5 ATP each, FADH₂=1.5 each. Total ≈ 36-38.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Angiotensin II causes:
questions.explanation: Angiotensin II: powerful vasoconstrictor, stimulates aldosterone secretion from adrenal cortex → Na⁺/water retention → increases BP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Biological control of pests uses:
questions.explanation: Biocontrol: using natural enemies of pests. e.g., Ladybird beetles eat aphids, Bt toxin kills bollworm, Trichoderma controls plant pathogens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Genomic imprinting means:
options: Expression of gene depends on which parent it was inherited from
questions.explanation: Genomic imprinting: some genes are expressed only from maternal or paternal allele (the other is silenced by methylation). Parent-of-origin effect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hayflick limit refers to:
options: Maximum number of times a normal cell can divide (~50)
questions.explanation: Hayflick limit: normal human cells divide about 50 times before entering senescence (due to telomere shortening). Cancer cells bypass this.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first cell of sporophytic generation in angiosperms is:
questions.explanation: Zygote (2n) is the first cell of sporophytic generation. It's formed by fusion of haploid gametes (syngamy) and divides to form embryo.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Alternation of generations is found in:
questions.explanation: Alternation of generations (gametophyte ↔ sporophyte) occurs in ALL plants. Relative dominance varies: bryophytes (gametophyte dominant), others (sporophyte dominant).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term 'immunity' that is present from birth is called:
questions.explanation: Innate (natural) immunity: present from birth, non-specific, includes physical barriers (skin), phagocytes, NK cells, complement, interferons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Guttation occurs through:
questions.explanation: Guttation: loss of water as liquid droplets through hydathodes (water pores) at leaf margins. Occurs when root pressure is high and transpiration is low.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Endemic species are those which are:
options: Confined to a particular geographic region
questions.explanation: Endemic species: found only in a specific geographical area and nowhere else. e.g., Lemurs (Madagascar), Kangaroos (Australia).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that synthesizes RNA primer during DNA replication is:
questions.explanation: Primase (RNA polymerase) synthesizes short RNA primer (8-12 nucleotides) required by DNA polymerase III to begin DNA synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Allergic reactions are mediated by:
questions.explanation: Allergy: IgE binds to mast cells → re-exposure to allergen → mast cell degranulation → histamine release → allergic symptoms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bolting (rapid stem elongation) is promoted by:
questions.explanation: Bolting: rapid internode elongation (especially in rosette plants) stimulated by gibberellins. Often precedes flowering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gene therapy for ADA deficiency involves introducing:
options: Functional ADA gene into patient's lymphocytes
questions.explanation: ADA (adenosine deaminase) gene therapy: functional ADA gene delivered via retroviral vector into patient's lymphocytes → produces enzyme → cures SCID.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hot spots of biodiversity are characterized by:
options: High endemism and high degree of threat
questions.explanation: Biodiversity hotspots (Norman Myers): areas with ≥1500 endemic plant species AND lost ≥70% original habitat. 34 hotspots globally. India has 4.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cranial nerve is responsible for facial expressions?
questions.explanation: Facial nerve (CN VII): motor innervation of facial muscles (expressions), taste sensation from anterior 2/3 tongue, salivary/lacrimal gland secretion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Quantitative trait loci (QTL) mapping is used to study:
questions.explanation: QTL mapping: identifies chromosomal regions (loci) containing genes that control quantitative/polygenic traits (height, yield, weight).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Autophagy is the process of:
options: Cell eating its own damaged organelles
questions.explanation: Autophagy: cellular self-eating. Damaged organelles enclosed in autophagosomes → fuse with lysosomes → digested. Important in cellular quality control.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Progesterone is called the 'pregnancy hormone' because it:
options: Maintains the endometrium for implantation and supports pregnancy
questions.explanation: Progesterone: maintains thick endometrium, inhibits uterine contractions, supports pregnancy. Drop in progesterone causes menstruation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Eutrophication leads to:
options: Algal bloom → decreased O₂ → fish kill
questions.explanation: Eutrophication: excess nutrients (N, P) → algal bloom → blocks light → algae die → decomposition uses O₂ → anoxia → fish death.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cytokinin promotes:
questions.explanation: Cytokinins: promote cell division (cytokinesis), delay leaf senescence, promote lateral bud growth (counteracts apical dominance by auxin).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Synovial fluid is found in:
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid: viscous fluid in synovial (diarthroses) joints. Acts as lubricant, shock absorber, and provides nutrients to cartilage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Epigenetics involves heritable changes that:
options: Do not change DNA sequence (methylation, histone modification)
questions.explanation: Epigenetics: heritable changes in gene expression without altering DNA sequence. Mechanisms: DNA methylation, histone modification, non-coding RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Binomial nomenclature was given by:
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature (two-part Latin name: Genus + species). His work 'Systema Naturae' (1758) established this system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Na⁺-K⁺ ATPase pump moves:
options: 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in (against concentration gradient)
questions.explanation: Na⁺/K⁺ pump: pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ into the cell per ATP hydrolyzed. Creates electrochemical gradient (electrogenic pump).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) deals with:
questions.explanation: Kyoto Protocol: international treaty to reduce greenhouse gas emissions (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) to combat global warming/climate change.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Southern blotting is used to detect:
questions.explanation: Southern blot (Edward Southern): detects specific DNA. Northern blot: RNA. Western blot: proteins. Uses probe hybridization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Archegonium is the female sex organ found in:
questions.explanation: Archegonium (flask-shaped female reproductive organ): present in bryophytes, pteridophytes, and gymnosperms. Absent in angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cushing's syndrome is caused by:
questions.explanation: Cushing's syndrome: excess cortisol (from adrenal cortex or exogenous). Symptoms: moon face, buffalo hump, obesity, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Genetic counselling is recommended for:
options: Couples with family history of genetic disorders
questions.explanation: Genetic counselling: for families with history of genetic disorders, consanguineous marriages, advanced maternal age, repeated miscarriages.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ubiquitin tags proteins for:
questions.explanation: Ubiquitin: small protein that marks damaged/old proteins for degradation by 26S proteasome. Ubiquitin-proteasome pathway regulates protein turnover.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Miller-Urey experiment (1953) demonstrated:
options: Abiotic synthesis of amino acids from inorganic molecules
questions.explanation: Miller-Urey: electric discharge through CH₄, NH₃, H₂, H₂O (primitive atmosphere simulation) produced amino acids abiotically, supporting chemical evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Serum differs from plasma in that it lacks:
questions.explanation: Serum = Plasma - clotting factors (fibrinogen). When blood clots, fibrinogen is converted to fibrin → removed → remaining liquid is serum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Emergency contraceptive pills must be taken within:
questions.explanation: Emergency contraceptive pills (levonorgestrel): effective within 72 hours (3 days) of unprotected intercourse. Prevent/delay ovulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chipko movement was started for:
questions.explanation: Chipko movement (1974, Garhwal Himalayas): villagers hugged trees to prevent cutting. Led by Sundarlal Bahuguna. Successful community-based conservation.
